title: The last evening
intro: At 9:20 p.m., a scream brings you to the study. Your host, Edmund Ashcroft, is dead. Minutes earlier, lightning plunged the estate into darkness. A fallen oak blocks the road, the telephone is down, and six guests must remain until morning. One of them is lying.
objective: Find who killed Ashcroft, which weapon they used, and where the murder happened. Search rooms, compare witness accounts, and follow the evidence behind the house’s supposed haunting.

rooms.name: Study
rooms.description: At 9:20 p.m., you found your host, Edmund Ashcroft, beside his overturned desk. The storm rattles the shutters. A dark stain marks the rug; the body has been covered with a sheet.

objects.name: Search the writing desk
objects.description: Beneath a blotter is a letter addressed to Colonel Mustard. A small brass cufflink lies caught in a splinter of the desk.

objects.name: Read the unfinished letter
objects.description: “Colonel: repay the money taken from the veterans’ fund by morning, or I deliver the ledger to the police.” The letter is signed Edmund Ashcroft.

objects.name: Follow the hidden passage
objects.description: The passage runs from the conservatory to a panel beside the study fireplace. In its dust, a heavy bootprint has a triangular gap at the heel.

rooms.name: Hall
rooms.description: The front doors are bolted against the storm. Beyond them, a fallen oak blocks the only road. Three soft knocks seem to come from inside an old portrait.

objects.name: Investigate the knocking portrait
objects.description: A loose shutter cord knocks against the wall. Pulling it shifts the portrait and exposes a diagram of a service passage between the conservatory and study. The ghost has a practical explanation.

objects.name: Examine the hall clock
objects.description: The clock is running correctly. The guest book beside it records dinner at 8:30 and Ashcroft’s private appointments at 9:00.

rooms.name: Lounge
rooms.description: The last embers glow beneath a marble mantel. Miss Scarlet left her glass near the piano when the lights went out.

objects.name: Inspect the revolver case
objects.description: The display revolver is still secured by its intact wax seal. All six chambers are empty, and there is no smell of fired powder.

objects.name: Read the marked sheet music
objects.description: A penciled note on the music reads “9:10 — Peacock joins me.” The piano bench holds room for two.

rooms.name: Library
rooms.description: A lamp illuminates Professor Plum’s research notes. A pocket watch lies open between two heavy books.

objects.name: Examine the pocket watch
objects.description: The glass cracked when Plum dropped his watch during the blackout. It stopped at 9:15. From here, the study wall is only a few feet away.

objects.name: Read the veterans’ ledger
objects.description: The accounts list transfers authorized by Mustard to a private account. Ashcroft has circled the missing funds in red.

rooms.name: Billiard Room
rooms.description: An unfinished game waits under a swaying green lamp. A repair kit has been left beside the radiator.

objects.name: Inspect the lead pipe
objects.description: A short lead pipe rests in a repair tray. Both ends are wrapped in undisturbed cobwebs; dust covers its entire length.

objects.name: Read the signed receipt
objects.description: Mr. Green signed for a loan repayment at 8:45. Ashcroft wrote “paid in full” underneath.

rooms.name: Dining Room
rooms.description: Six places remain set around the abandoned dinner. One of the two silver candlesticks is missing; the other is still upright.

objects.name: Look beneath the sideboard
objects.description: Behind the sideboard lies the missing silver candlestick. Its base is dented and bears a dark stain. A violet wool fiber clings to an edge.

objects.name: Examine Mustard’s place setting
objects.description: A regimental jacket hangs on Mustard’s chair. One cufflink is missing, and its violet wool sleeve has a fresh tear. The jacket itself stays where you found it.

rooms.name: Conservatory
rooms.description: Rain drums on the glass roof. Mud crosses the tiles toward a bookcase that seems oddly shallow.

objects.name: Inspect the garden rope
objects.description: The coiled rope is wet with rain and green with plant sap. The loop around a hanging planter is still tied tightly.

objects.name: Examine the muddy boots
objects.description: A pair of boots marked “C. Mustard” stands by the door. A triangular piece is missing from the left heel.

rooms.name: Ballroom
rooms.description: Chandeliers tremble whenever thunder rolls. A toolbox sits beside the mechanism of a silent mechanical organ.

objects.name: Inspect the wrench
objects.description: The wrench fits the organ’s loose crank. It is covered in sticky oil, but the pale dust on its handle shows no recent grip.

objects.name: Read the evening programme
objects.description: Ashcroft invited everyone to hear a new recording at 9:30. A handwritten addition says he intended to make “an announcement about the fund.”

rooms.name: Kitchen
rooms.description: Mrs. White’s kettle is still warm. A knife rack and a tray of unserved desserts sit beneath a single lamp.

objects.name: Inspect the dagger
objects.description: The decorative dagger used to cut the cake is sticky with raspberry glaze. Mrs. White’s recipe card calls for exactly that filling.

objects.name: Examine the tea tray
objects.description: A tea order in Mrs. White’s hand reads “9:12 — Green helping with kettle.” Two used cups stand beside it.

passages.name: The ghost walk
passages.description: You work the latch the portrait’s diagram showed you. The panel opens onto a narrow stone passage behind the library wall, cold and smelling of rain. Fresh mud runs the whole way between the conservatory bookcase and the study fireplace.

events.name: Knocking in the walls
events.text: As you step into the hall, every candle leans the same way. Three slow knocks answer your footsteps from behind the old portrait, then stop the moment you turn toward it.

events.name: Something inside the wall
events.text: The lamp gutters. From behind the shelves comes a slow scrape, like a boot dragged over stone, moving along the inside of the outer wall toward the study. When the light steadies, the sound is gone.

events.name: The bookcase breathes
events.text: Lightning whitens the glass roof. In the flash the shallow bookcase seems to breathe: a cold draft stirs the ferns beside it and carries the smell of old stone, though every window is shut.

events.name: Footsteps in the passage
events.text: As you step back from the panel, it swings shut with a soft click. Footsteps seem to retreat down the dark passage, then fade. It is only your own echo, but someone walked that passage tonight in heavier boots than yours.

clues.title: Regimental cufflink
clues.description: A brass cufflink bearing Colonel Mustard’s regimental crest was caught in the freshly splintered desk.

clues.title: Ashcroft’s ultimatum
clues.description: Ashcroft planned to report Mustard’s theft from the veterans’ fund the following morning.

clues.title: A distinctive bootprint
clues.description: A fresh bootprint leads into the study from the conservatory. Its heel has a triangular gap.

clues.title: The portrait’s secret
clues.description: The knocking comes from a shutter cord. A diagram shows how to open the hidden passage between the conservatory and study.

clues.title: Private appointments
clues.description: Ashcroft arranged to see each guest privately after dinner, beginning at 9:00 p.m.

clues.title: Revolver
clues.description: The unloaded revolver remains behind an intact wax seal. There is no evidence that it was fired.

clues.title: A penciled time
clues.description: Scarlet’s sheet music records Mrs. Peacock joining her at the piano at 9:10. A note alone is not independent proof.

clues.title: The stopped watch
clues.description: Plum’s watch stopped at 9:15 during the blackout, shortly before Ashcroft was discovered at 9:20.

clues.title: The missing funds
clues.description: The veterans’ fund ledger records unexplained transfers authorized by Colonel Mustard.

clues.title: Lead pipe
clues.description: The pipe’s dust and cobwebs are undisturbed, suggesting it has not been handled tonight.

clues.title: A settled debt
clues.description: Ashcroft acknowledged Green’s debt as paid in full at 8:45, before the murder.

clues.title: Dented candlestick
clues.description: A dented candlestick bears a dark stain and a violet wool fiber. Its partner remains on the dinner table.

clues.title: The torn violet sleeve
clues.description: Mustard’s violet wool jacket has a torn sleeve and a missing regimental cufflink.

clues.title: Rope
clues.description: The garden rope is still supporting a heavy planter. It is wet and stained with plant sap.

clues.title: Mustard’s damaged boots
clues.description: Boots marked C. Mustard have a triangular gap in the left heel.

clues.title: Wrench
clues.description: The oily wrench has undisturbed dust on its handle. No matching oil marks were visible around the study desk.

clues.title: An interrupted announcement
clues.description: Ashcroft planned a public announcement about the veterans’ fund at 9:30.

clues.title: Dagger
clues.description: The dagger bears raspberry glaze from the cake. Its blade and point show no other visible stains.

clues.title: The late tea order
clues.description: White’s written tea order places Green helping in the kitchen at 9:12, shortly before the blackout.

clues.title: Footsteps in the wall
clues.description: Something moved inside the library’s outer wall, heading toward the study. There is a hollow space there that the floor plan does not show.

clues.title: A draft behind the bookcase
clues.description: Cold air flows from behind the conservatory bookcase, exactly where the muddy trail ends. There is open space behind it.

clues.title: Scarlet’s account
clues.description: Scarlet says she and Peacock were at the lounge piano from 9:10 until the body was found.

clues.title: Mustard left dinner
clues.description: Scarlet saw Mustard walk toward the conservatory at about 9:10.

clues.title: Mustard’s claim
clues.description: Mustard claims he stayed in the dining room all evening and never entered the study.

clues.title: Mustard acknowledges the cufflink
clues.description: Mustard recognizes the study cufflink as his, but says it was lost on an earlier visit.

clues.title: The borrowed funds
clues.description: Mustard admits taking the charity money and being threatened with exposure by morning.

clues.title: A changed account
clues.description: Confronted with the matching heel, Mustard admits entering the study through the hidden passage.

clues.title: White’s kitchen account
clues.description: White says she and Green were in the kitchen together during the blackout.

clues.title: The missing table ornament
clues.description: White saw both candlesticks at dinner at 9:05. A candlestick was later hidden under the dining-room sideboard.

clues.title: Who knew the ghost walk
clues.description: White says Mustard knew the service passage from earlier private meetings with Ashcroft.

clues.title: Green’s kitchen account
clues.description: Green independently places himself with White in the kitchen from about 9:10.

clues.title: Green’s settled business
clues.description: Green says the receipt settled his debt at 8:45.

clues.title: A fresh tear
clues.description: Green says Mustard’s violet sleeve was intact on arrival and torn after the scream.

clues.title: Peacock corroborates Scarlet
clues.description: Peacock independently confirms staying with Scarlet at the lounge piano during the blackout.

clues.title: A thud at the quarter hour
clues.description: Peacock heard a heavy thud from the study at approximately 9:15, followed by footsteps toward the dining room.

clues.title: Plum’s account
clues.description: Plum says he was alone in the library and heard a heavy impact through the study wall during the blackout.

clues.title: Plum’s observation of the injury
clues.description: Plum reports one broad injury to the back of Ashcroft’s head and no visible puncture or gunshot wound. This is a witness observation, not a medical examination.

clues.title: Violet wool comparison
clues.description: Plum observes that the candlestick fiber resembles Mustard’s torn violet wool sleeve.

suspects.name: Miss Scarlet
suspects.greeting: Edmund invited us for dinner, then spent the evening threatening people. Ask what you need. I want this over before dawn.

topics.prompt: Where were you during the blackout?
topics.reply: I was at the lounge piano from 9:05 until the scream. Mrs. Peacock joined me at 9:10; we stayed together.

topics.prompt: Why did Ashcroft invite you?
topics.reply: I was buying his late wife’s paintings. He raised the price over dinner, and I was furious. That is hardly a reason to kill him.

topics.prompt: Did anyone leave the dining room?
topics.reply: At about 9:10 I saw Mustard leave toward the conservatory. He said he needed air. I did not see him return.

suspects.name: Colonel Mustard
suspects.greeting: Keep your questions brief. A storm and a dead host are quite enough unpleasantness for one evening.

topics.prompt: Where were you at 9:15?
topics.reply: In the dining room, all evening after dinner. I never entered the study tonight.

topics.prompt: What business did you have with Ashcroft?
topics.reply: I administered his veterans’ charity. We disagreed about the accounts. A bookkeeping dispute, nothing more.

topics.prompt: Why was your cufflink in the study?
topics.reply: That is my crest. I must have lost it on an earlier visit. I certainly did not struggle with Edmund tonight.

topics.prompt: What about the ultimatum and missing funds?
topics.reply: I borrowed the money. I meant to replace it. Edmund would not listen; he said he would ruin me by morning.

topics.prompt: Your boot matches the passage print. Explain.
topics.reply: I went through the conservatory passage to speak to him. Yes, I lied about staying at dinner. But entering that room does not prove I killed him.

suspects.name: Mrs. White
suspects.greeting: I have kept this house for twenty years. Tonight even the walls sound restless. Still, people do more harm than ghosts.

topics.prompt: Where were you when the lights went out?
topics.reply: In the kitchen with Mr. Green. He was helping lift the kettle when the lights failed.

topics.prompt: How did you get along with Ashcroft?
topics.reply: He was selling the estate. I would have lost my job. But he had written me a reference, and I was already packing.

topics.prompt: When did you last see both candlesticks?
topics.reply: Both were on the dinner table when I cleared the plates at 9:05. I passed the study at 9:18; through the door I saw only the fallen desk lamp.

topics.prompt: Do you know about the hidden passage?
topics.reply: The family called it the ghost walk. It connects the conservatory to the study. Mustard used it on earlier visits to discuss the charity privately.

suspects.name: Mr. Green
suspects.greeting: I know what everyone thinks about my debts. Check the papers before you decide who I am.

topics.prompt: Can anyone confirm your whereabouts?
topics.reply: Mrs. White. I helped her in the kitchen from about 9:10 until we heard the scream.

topics.prompt: Was your debt a reason to threaten Ashcroft?
topics.reply: It was paid at 8:45. He signed the receipt himself. I came to dinner owing him nothing.

topics.prompt: Did you notice Mustard’s jacket?
topics.reply: He took it off after the scream. I noticed a rip in that violet sleeve. It was whole when he arrived for dinner.

suspects.name: Mrs. Peacock
suspects.greeting: Edmund loved a captive audience. Now the storm has made us exactly that. I will tell you what I saw.

topics.prompt: Where did you spend the evening?
topics.reply: With Miss Scarlet at the lounge piano after 9:10. When the lights went out, we held hands until they came back.

topics.prompt: Did you have a disagreement with Ashcroft?
topics.reply: He threatened to withdraw his donation to my hospital. Cruel, yes. But the hospital could survive without his money.

topics.prompt: What did you hear during the blackout?
topics.reply: One heavy thud from the study, just as the hall clock finished striking the quarter hour. Then footsteps toward the dining room.

suspects.name: Professor Plum
suspects.greeting: I was reading in the library. The dead deserve facts, so let us distinguish observations from rumors.

topics.prompt: What happened during the blackout?
topics.reply: I was alone in the library. I dropped my watch when the lights failed. I heard a single heavy impact through the study wall.

topics.prompt: Why were you invited here?
topics.reply: Ashcroft owned letters I needed for my research. He refused to let me publish them. We argued before dinner, in front of everyone.

topics.prompt: What did you observe when the body was found?
topics.reply: A single broad injury at the back of the head. No visible puncture or gunshot wound. A heavy blunt object would fit what I saw.

topics.prompt: Does this fiber resemble the torn sleeve?
topics.reply: The fiber on the candlestick and Mustard’s torn sleeve appear to be the same violet wool. Compare that with the cufflink in the study.

solution.explanation: Colonel Mustard killed Edmund Ashcroft in the study with the dining-room candlestick at about 9:15. Ashcroft was about to expose his theft from the veterans’ fund. Mustard entered through the conservatory passage, leaving his distinctive bootprint, and lost a cufflink in the struggle. His torn violet sleeve left a fiber on the candlestick. During the blackout he struck Ashcroft, then hid the weapon under the dining-room sideboard and claimed he had never left dinner. The knocking behind the portrait was a loose shutter cord; the house’s ghost story concealed a human route.
